segments.title: Chương 263: 0265 【Thân phận mới của Trần Quý Lương: Đồng hành khoa học và trò chuyện】
segments.content:
Chapter 268-0265 Chen Guiliang's New Identity: Research Chat Companion

Professor Lin didn't get on the back of the bicycle, but had Chen Guiliang push it and walk with him.

At this time, due to the lack of proper parking spaces at Peking University, the problem of disorderly parking was very serious.

From time to time, students would complain that the teachers' private cars had taken over the open space in front of the academic buildings, leaving them with nowhere to park their bicycles.

In reality, it was against the rules to park any vehicle there. Including bicycles.

Carrying his briefcase, Professor Lin walked and asked, "Those questions you raised, which professor's book did you read? Professor Wu, Professor Zhang, or... Professor Li?"

Chen Guiliang said, "I've attended some lectures by Professor Li and Professor Zhang, but their course content isn't the reason for my questions. It's inevitable that infrastructure and real estate will get out of control. It's already very difficult for the central government to regulate, unless it makes a clean break and returns to the past."

Professor Lin said, "You are very pessimistic about the future."

"I don't know much about economics, but I understand some things about human nature," Chen Guiliang said. "My middle school teachers couldn't get their salaries and could only make ends meet by forcing students into remedial classes during summer vacation. But the students all came from the countryside, and some would rather drop out of school than pay the remedial fees. This is the result of local financial difficulties caused by the tax-sharing system; the county simply can't produce the money. Now that they can make money by selling land, what do you think the county leaders will do, Professor Lin?"

Professor Lin said, "Sell, sell, and sell some more."

Chen Guiliang continued, "When the vast majority of local governments across the country rely on selling land to supplement their finances, then the government, banks, real estate developers, and upstream and downstream enterprises will all be tied to this high-speed train."

Professor Lin asked, "You think a real estate bubble will emerge?"

Chen Guiliang shook his head, "A bubble is just the result. It's easy to go from frugal to extravagant, but hard to go from extravagant to frugal. If local governments all rely on land sales to fill their coffers, they will definitely go all out on infrastructure development. It brings political achievements, a good reputation, and opportunities for rent-seeking."

"In this situation, how can the central government regulate it? On what grounds? When this is happening all over the country, the debt a single county carries might take its local fiscal revenue decades to pay off. How much debt would that be for the entire country combined?"

"When housing prices are driven higher and higher, and people see that they only go up and never down, it will slowly evolve into panic buying. The higher they rise, the more people buy, and the more people buy, the higher they rise. At that point, a young man from the countryside won't even be qualified to get married if he doesn't buy a house in the city."

"For the so-called middle class, when they spend a few million on a house, they will subconsciously think they are rich. Even if they are still carrying many loans and are up to their ears in debt, they will still feel they are rich. And rich people need to have high consumption, so the era of advance consumption will also arrive. This is especially true for the next generation of young people; they will find it very difficult to save money..."

"This development model for real estate won't just affect the economy, but every aspect of society. The entire society's way of thinking will shift..."

"When China's economy reaches a bottleneck, with fewer and fewer opportunities to get ahead and social classes becoming more and more rigid, what will happen? For the majority of young people, it won't matter how hard they work. They won't be able to afford a house anyway."

"At that point, you'll see a decline in the desire to marry, a drop in the birth rate, the arrival of negative population growth, and accelerated aging... China's entire demographic structure will become unbalanced, leading to a series of even more serious social and economic problems."

Professor Lin listened to Chen Guiliang seriously and said in a solemn tone, "You discuss real estate from the perspective of social impact. This angle is very novel, and it's given me a lot of inspiration. But your predictions are all very pessimistic and extreme."

Chen Guiliang said, "The more extreme the housing prices become, the more it will force the entire society to become extreme. Ordinary people have no choice. All they know is that housing prices are getting higher and higher, and if they don't buy soon, they will keep rising. When the whole nation is focused on housing prices, the first thing a mother-in-law will look for in a prospective son-in-law is whether he has a house."

"Then there's the rising cost of education, which is already starting to show. In the future, to raise a child, you'll have to sign them up for all sorts of training classes, to not let your child lose at the starting line. It's possible that before they even finish primary school, you'll have thrown over a hundred thousand into their education expenses."

"Moreover, with the development of the internet, entertainment options are becoming more and more diverse. If everyone can get online, and internet access is cheap, young people will become more isolated and withdrawn. They might even find romance uninteresting."

"Combine that with the difficulty of buying a house, getting married, and raising children, and in the future, more and more young people will definitely marry late or not at all. They would rather immerse themselves in the virtual world of the internet. Negative population growth is inevitable, and the early arrival of an aging population is also inevitable."

Professor Lin carefully considered these remarks. He found Chen Guiliang's ideas more and more interesting.

This was because the people he usually interacted with and debated, aside from leaders and entrepreneurs, were mostly renowned scholars in the field of economics.

Those scholars who opposed over-reliance on infrastructure and real estate did so entirely from an economic perspective. For instance, it would lead to diminishing returns on capital, squeeze out consumption, waste resources, cause debt problems, and lead to corruption, and so on...

But everything Chen Guiliang talked about were social problems.

And when society has problems, it will inevitably trigger economic problems!

Professor Lin decided to communicate more with sociologists in the future. This was another direction for studying economics.

Professor Lin said, "This development model is already unstoppable. It doesn't matter who says what; we can only try our best to regulate it and apply the brakes. We have to wait until China's industrial scale is large enough, when qualitative change leads to quantitative change, and the state guides industrial upgrading. Only then can we reduce our reliance on real estate."

The entrance to the underground parking garage was just ahead.

Professor Lin stopped and said, "Peking University students who want to be recommended to CCER need to take related elective courses in their sophomore year and establish a connection with their future advisor. In their junior year, they can try to become a CCER research assistant. You are a junior now and have enrolled in my class. If you want to be recommended to CCER, you can write a research assistant application."

"Thank you for thinking highly of me, Professor Lin, but I really don't have the time," Chen Guiliang said.

CCER's graduate students used a dual-advisor system, one Chinese and one foreign.

The foreign advisor would certainly teach entirely in English, and one would also need to understand professional English in the field of economics. That kind of professional English was much more difficult than passing the CET-6.

If Chen Guiliang had the energy to study professional economics English, he might as well spend that effort investing in a couple more companies.

Professor Lin wasn't in a hurry to get to the garage either. He smiled and said, "Do all of you who work in the internet industry see things from such a peculiar angle?"

Chen Guiliang said, "This isn't from the perspective of an internet professional, but from a philosophical one. For many of my courses, I need the teachers to go easy on me just to avoid failing. But for the philosophy courses I enrolled in, I passed them all on my own merit."

"But you are in the internet industry, so you must have thought deeply about its development, right?" Professor Lin said. "This year, China's internet has entered an era of venture madness, which has attracted the attention of many economists. I happen to be following the internet as well and would like to chat with you about it."

Chen Guiliang asked, "What would you like to talk about, Professor Lin?"

Professor Lin said, "Your views on the future development of the internet."

Chen Guiliang said, "Now and in the future, there will only be two major internet hubs in the whole world. One is China, and the other is the United States. There will be no others."

Professor Lin smiled, "If you were to expand on that viewpoint, you could write a master's thesis. What else?"

Chen Guiliang said, "The internet will become more and more personalized, centered around the user. I'm very much looking forward to the era of the Internet of Everything."

"The Internet of Everything?" Professor Lin didn't understand.

Chen Guiliang said, "Everything from public facilities to personal furniture, all connected to the internet!"

Professor Lin thought about it carefully. "That statement is very sci-fi."
